title: STILL PRESENT (r1): W3 — corrected_at stale-bounce gate compares RFC3339 vs Postgres ::text lexically; same-day redelivered pre-correction failure exhausts + stamps referee_contact_invalid
evidence: webhooks.gleam:303-304: "// ISO timestamps — lexical compare is chronological." / "string.compare(at, corrected) != order.Lt"; find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql:35-42: "SELECT e->>'at' ... AS matched_send_at" / "COALESCE(rc.corrected_at::text, '') AS corrected_at"; sweep.gleam:180: "|> timestamp.to_rfc3339(calendar.utc_offset)" (attempts at = RFC3339 'T'/'Z'); psql on the live test DB: SELECT '2026-08-01T08:00:00Z' > '2026-08-01 19:50:25.594426+00' -> t (timestamptz::text is ' ' / '+00'); pin fixture line 957: "[{\"at\":\"2026-08-01T08:00:00Z\",..."}
detail: On the same calendar day 'T'(0x54) > ' '(0x20) makes every RFC3339 send time lexically GREATER than every Postgres-text correction time, so a same-day redelivered pre-correction bounce (W3's exact case) is treated as genuine: row exhausts to unreachable + fabricated referee_contact_invalid (AC3b). Cross-day stands down only by digit luck; the pin test passes only because fixture date 2026-08-01 < run date 2026-08-12 (suite green today, would fail on/before 08-01).
recommended_fix: Compare timestamps, not strings: return a boolean from the SQL (e.g. (e->>'at')::timestamptz > rc.corrected_at AS is_post_correction) or parse both sides in Gleam; drop the lexical-compare comment.
